notes: rounds/tester.py result() checks the round is Open and the build current, reads the tester's own result, refuses a POST to a submitted one and renders a submitted one without a form; write_result re-checks Open under the round lock, and services.save_result re-checks Open, the current build, the tester's own row and submitted_at. M1 drops the tester filter in both reads; M3 lets all three Open checks pass a Closed round; M4 removes the three submitted checks, lets tester_result.html show the form for a submitted result and prints its real status there (a save keeps submitted_at, so it stays Submitted). ResultForm.clean requires a Fail observation (no database constraint); M5 raises only ObservationField's max_length, so OBSERVATION_LENGTH still says 2000. M3 leaves the tester round page's Open-only 'Record result' link in place (navigation, not a guard). M5 also widens the model field and its column in migration 0005_result to 2001, together, because the varchar(2000) column would otherwise refuse the save (a 503) and a model-only change would fail the candidate's makemigrations --check test; pytest-django builds the test database from migrations on every run (no --reuse-db), so the migration edit is seen consistently.
